method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Use an aseptic technique for all wound care**; irrigate to decontaminate before dressing, and give adequate analgesia.
claims.source_text: All wound care including cleaning, irrigation and dressings should be managed with an aseptic technique … Initial decontamination of the wound with irrigation is of utmost importance and should be performed prior to dressing … Provide adequate analgesia during wound care
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for nerve, vessel and tendon damage**, testing movement while exploring — especially palmar and hand wounds.
claims.source_text: underlying nerve, vessel and tendon damage. This requires assessment of movement while exploring the wound (especially in palmar or hand wounds
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **X-ray** for fracture or a radiopaque foreign body (glass, metal); **ultrasound** for a puncture with a radiolucent one (thorn, splinter). **Swab only if considering antibiotics.**
claims.source_text: Consider X-ray for underlying fracture or radiopaque foreign body eg glass or metal … Consider ultrasound for puncture wounds with a radiolucent foreign body eg thorn or splinter … Consider swab for MCS only if considering antibiotics
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antiseptic irrigation can damage tissue defences and slow healing** — except contaminated wounds, which may benefit from **chlorhexidine 0.05% or povidone-iodine 1%** irrigation.
claims.source_text: Cleansing/irrigating with antiseptics may damage tissue defences and impede healing. The exception is contaminated wounds that may benefit from chlorhexidine 0.05% or povidine-iodine 1% irrigation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Irrigate with 0.9% sodium chloride from a 20–30 mL syringe and large-bore non-bevelled needle**, held just above the wound with continuous gentle pressure; **about 50–100 mL per cm of wound.**
claims.source_text: Use a 20-30 mL syringe with a large bore non bevelled needle filled with 0.9% sodium chloride to slowly irrigate the wound … Hold the syringe just above the top edge of the wound using continuous gentle pressure to flush fluid … Thorough irrigation (eg 50-100mL per cm length of wound) is required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer to plastics or general surgery** (in ED or as outpatient) for cosmetically sensitive wounds, deep wounds or significant tissue loss, and injury to tendons, nerves or vessels.
claims.source_text: Consider referral for plastic or general surgical opinion either in ED or as outpatient for: cosmetically sensitive wounds deep wounds or wounds with significant tissue loss involvement of underlying structures such as tendons, nerves and vessels
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most wounds do not need antibiotics**; decontamination matters more.
claims.source_text: Most wounds do not require antibiotic therapy Initial decontamination of wound is more important
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Reserve antibiotics for:** animal or human bites · penetrating wounds of vital structures (e.g. eye) · contaminated wounds, especially deep · severe or contaminated water wounds · **cleaning delayed over 8 hours** · extensive tissue damage or massive contamination.
claims.source_text: Antibiotics should be reserved for: animal/human bites penetrating wounds of vital structures (eg eye) contaminated wounds especially when deep severe or contaminated water-wounds when wound cleaning has been delayed (> 8 hours) wounds with extensive tissue damage or massive contamination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **By healing stage:** hydrogels for debridement; low-adherent moisture-maintaining for granulation; low-adherent for epithelialisation.
claims.source_text: Hydrogels for debridement stage Low adherent moisture maintaining for granulation stage Low adherent for epithelialisation stage
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Grazes and abrasions:** keep dry. Clean — film, tulle, fixation sheet or dry; soiled — dry or tulle. **Review at 2 days.**
claims.source_text: Graze, abrasions - clean Keep dry Film, tulle, fixation sheet or dry 2 days Graze, abrasions - soiled Keep dry Dry or tulle 2 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Closed lacerations (sutured or glued):** protect, open or dry, paper-tape support after suture removal; **review 3–7 days.** **Puncture wounds:** keep dry and visible, open or dry; **review 1–2 days.**
claims.source_text: Lacerations - sutured/ glued/ closed Protect and minimise irritation Open or dry, consider paper tape support following suture removal 3-7 days Puncture wounds Keep dry, allow visualisation of wound Open or dry 1-2 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infected wound:** antimicrobial, moist healing; **avoid semi-occlusive dressings**, consider alginate or hydrocolloid if exudate is high; **review 1–2 days.**
claims.source_text: Infected wound Antimicrobial. Moist healing. Odour absorption Avoid semi occlusive dressings. Consider alginate or hydrocolloid if high exudate 1-2 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Slough:** dry — moisture retention (hydrocolloid, semi-permeable); moist — absorbent (alginate, foam).
claims.source_text: Slough - dry Hydration. Control moisture balance. Promote debridement Moisture retention eg hydrocolloid, semi permeable Slough - moist Fluid absorption. Protect surrounding skin. Promote debridement Absorbent dressing eg alginate, foam
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Semi-permeable film** (OpSite, Tegaderm): superficial wounds or as a secondary dressing; **not for highly exudative wounds.**
claims.source_text: Semi-permeable Thin, adhesive, transparent polyurethrane film OpSite, Tegaderm Allows inspection. Self-adhesive. Some moisture evaporation. Reduces pain. Barrier to external contamination Exudate may pool. May be traumatic to remove. Surrounding skin may become macerated Superficial wounds. As a secondary dressing Highly exudative wounds
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fixation sheet** (Fixomull, Hypafix, Mefix): changes can be left 5–7 days; wash with soap and water and pat dry twice daily; **oil before removal**. Not for infected wounds or adhesive allergy.
claims.source_text: Fixation Sheet Porous polyester fabric with adhesive backing Fixomull, Hypafix, Mefix Can be used directly on wound site … Dressing changes can be left for 5-7 days Dressing needs washing with soap and water, pat-dried twice daily. Requires application of oil prior to removal, ideally soaked in oil and wrapped in cling film overnight … Infected wounds. Allergy to adhesives
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Calcium alginate** (Kaltostat): for moderate or high exudate and haemostasis; **not recommended in anaerobic infection**; the gel can be mistaken for slough or pus.
claims.source_text: Calcium Alginate Natural polysaccharide from seaweed Kaltostat Forms gel on wound … Not recommended in anaerobic infections. Gel can be confused with slough or pus in wound … Moderately or highly exudative wounds. Need for haemostasis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Antimicrobial dressings** (Acticoat, Aquacel Ag, Idosorb) for infected wounds and burns — **caution with iodine dressings in thyroid disease.**
claims.source_text: Antimicrobial Acticoat, Aquacel Ag, Idosorb Decrease bacterial load Expensive Infected wounds. Burns Caution use of iodine dressings in patients with thyroid disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Educate on healing, infection signs and scars:** avoid sun; **scar massage from 2–4 weeks after closure or suture removal, 5–10 min twice daily.**
claims.source_text: Provide education regarding wound healing, monitoring for signs of infection and scar minimisation strategies, including: Avoid sun exposure Scar massage from 2-4 weeks following wound closure/suture removal 5-10 min twice daily
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult surgery/plastics** if the dressing is too complex or the specific dressing is unavailable. **Discharge** once the dressing is on and follow-up is planned.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with surgical/plastics team when Wound dressing too complex to complete or specific dressings not available … Consider discharge when Dressing applied and follow-up plan in place
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Wound dressings - acute traumatic wounds' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Wound_dressings_acute_traumatic_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23
